story_type: tornado aftermath, downtown flattened, ground-level walk through a small city a week later
hook: Downtown Mayfield, one week after an EF4 tornado.
narration: This was downtown Mayfield, Kentucky, one week after a tornado went straight through it.
The storm began in far northwest Tennessee and kept going across western Kentucky.
Weather Service damage surveys rated it EF4, a violent tornado.
Its path ran one hundred sixty-five point seven miles, among the longest in U.S. history.
Surveyors rate a tornado by its damage. They match what failed, like a brick wall or a stand of trees, to the wind it takes to break it.
Downtown, whole brick fronts were torn open to the street.
On a fence, people left flowers and a sign that read Mayfield Strong.
In the neighborhoods, trees were stripped bare and houses were split apart.
outcome: One week later, excavators were clearing what the tornado left behind in Mayfield.
title: Tornado wrecked downtown Mayfield
description:
Downtown Mayfield, Kentucky, filmed by FEMA on Dec. 17, 2021, one week after a violent EF4 tornado crossed western Kentucky on one of the longest tornado paths in U.S. history.

Footage: FEMA video by Alexis Hall, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/826287/tornado-leaves-path-destruction-kentucky
